title: Fascia iliaca / femoral nerve block
stem: Cubicle 21. Mrs Ma, 84 (50 kg), has a fractured neck of femur. She is in severe pain despite paracetamol. Perform an ultrasound-guided fascia iliaca block on the model.

phases.title: Safety checks
phases.goal: Consent, her weight and the maximum dose, monitoring, lipid, no earlier block.

phases.title: Draw up
phases.goal: The right drug and volume from the cart.

phases.title: The block
phases.goal: By hand under ultrasound: the image, the anatomy, the needle under the fascia, the spread.

review.text: Local anaesthetic dose. Your notes give 20–30 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 0.25–0.5% bupivacaine. Check the total against weight: 30 mL of 0.5% is 150 mg, over 2 mg/kg in a 50 kg woman. Use a larger volume of a more dilute solution within the maximum dose, and label the patient with the drug and time.

notes:
Checked against NICE CG124 (Hip fracture, updated 2023), the Association of Anaesthetists / RCEM safety guideline for fascia iliaca blocks in the ED (2021), and the AAGBI guideline for local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST, 2010).

NICE recommends nerve blocks (fascia iliaca or femoral) for hip fracture pain in the ED, alongside paracetamol and cautious opioids. The ultrasound-guided fascia iliaca compartment block deposits a large volume of dilute local anaesthetic under the fascia iliaca, lateral to the femoral nerve, spreading to the femoral and lateral femoral cutaneous nerves (and sometimes obturator). Safety: consent, check allergies and anticoagulation, weight-based dose (e.g. levobupivacaine 0.25% up to 2 mg/kg, or 30–40 mL of a dilute solution staying within the maximum dose), monitoring, IV access, aspirate before injecting in 5 mL increments, lipid emulsion available, document, and a sign on the patient (time and drug) to avoid repeat dosing.

Your notes describe a femoral nerve block with 20–30 mL ropivacaine 0.5% or bupivacaine 0.25–0.5%; check the total dose against weight (0.5% × 30 mL = 150 mg — over 2 mg/kg in a 50 kg woman). The rest (NAVEL, in-plane, hydrodissection, aspiration, LAST readiness) matches.

opts.r: 200 mg is 4 mg/kg for 50 kg: toxic. Use 0.25% for volume within 2 mg/kg.
Too little volume to spread under the fascia: about 40 mL of dilute solution.
